quests.discovery: A checkpoint guard, cold, on a long night, asks for lamp oil. The checkpoint is not yours. The guard is cold. The lamp oil is yours. The lamp oil is for your shelter. The guard is the law at the checkpoint. The guard is cold. The cold is the guard. The lamp oil is the question.

choices.label: Give the lamp oil
choices.outcome_text: You give the lamp oil. The guard is warm, grateful. The checkpoint is easier now. The guard waves you through. The lamp oil is gone. The giving was the thing. The thing was the warmth for the guard.
choices.epitaph: Gave the lamp oil. The guard was warm. The giving was the thing. The warmth was the guard's.

choices.label: Trade the lamp oil for passage
choices.outcome_text: You trade the lamp oil for passage. The guard agrees. The trade is the thing. The thing is the deal. The deal is the lamp oil for the through. The through is the trade.
choices.epitaph: Traded the lamp oil for passage. The deal is the through. The through is the trade.

choices.label: Refuse, the oil is for the shelter
choices.outcome_text: You refuse. The oil is for the shelter. The guard nods. The guard is cold. The checkpoint is harder now. The refusing was the thing. The thing was the oil. The oil is the cold for the guard.
choices.epitaph: Refused. The oil is for the shelter. The guard is cold. The oil is the cold for the guard.

choices.label: Share a little, keep most
choices.outcome_text: You share a little, keep most. The guard is a little warmer. You have most of the oil. The sharing was the thing. The thing was the compromise. The compromise is the little.
choices.epitaph: Shared a little, kept most. The compromise is the little. The little was the thing.

quests.trigger: A child claims to be the heir of a dead leader, asking for shelter.
quests.discovery: A child, maybe twelve, claims to be the heir of a dead leader of a distant camp. The child has a token — a medallion, real-looking. The child asks for shelter, by right of the claim. The claim could be true. The claim could be a child's story. The token could be real. The token could be stolen. The child is a child. The claim is the question.

choices.label: Shelter the child, investigate the claim
choices.outcome_text: You shelter the child and investigate. The claim may be true. The child is a child. The sheltering was the thing. The thing was the not-turning-away. The not-turning-away is the child.
choices.epitaph: Sheltered the child, investigated. The not-turning-away is the child.

choices.label: Shelter the child, ignore the claim
choices.outcome_text: You shelter the child and ignore the claim. The child is a child. The claim is the claim. The sheltering is the thing. The thing is the child, not the claim. The claim is the not-the-thing.
choices.epitaph: Sheltered the child, ignored the claim. The child is the thing. The claim is not.

choices.label: Refuse, the claim is not your problem
choices.outcome_text: You refuse. The claim is not your problem. The child leaves, with the token. The child is a child. The refusing was the thing. The thing was the not-shelter. The not-shelter is the child in the road.
choices.epitaph: Refused. The child is in the road. The not-shelter is the thing. The claim was not my problem.

choices.label: Take the token, turn the child away
choices.outcome_text: You take the token and turn the child away. The token is real, maybe. The child is without the token now. The taking was the thing. The thing was the theft from a child. The theft is the token.
choices.epitaph: Took the token, turned the child away. The theft is the token. The thing is the theft from a child.

quests.trigger: A raider, wounded and dying, expresses remorse.
quests.discovery: A raider by the road, gut-shot and dying, tells you he did bad things and is sorry. His knife is still on his belt. You know the armband on his sleeve from two burned farms. The remorse may be real, or it may be the fear of the dark. He is waiting to see what you do with it.

choices.label: Listen to the remorse, offer comfort
choices.outcome_text: You listen and offer comfort: water, a word. He weeps into the dirt. When he dies you take the knife off his belt and leave the armband where it is.
choices.epitaph: Listened to the raider's remorse. Gave water and a word. I took the knife and left the armband.

choices.label: Listen, offer no comfort
choices.outcome_text: You listen and offer nothing. He talks until his voice gives out. He dies mid-sentence, asking whether it counts for something.
choices.epitaph: Listened and offered nothing. He asked if it counted. I did not answer.

choices.label: Refuse to listen, walk on
choices.outcome_text: You refuse to listen and walk on. Behind you he keeps talking for a while. Then the road is only the road.
choices.epitaph: Walked on. He kept talking for a while after.

choices.label: Listen, then judge them
choices.outcome_text: You listen, then tell him what he did was wrong. He nods. He knew. You are the last thing that speaks to him, and you spend it on a verdict.
choices.epitaph: Listened, then judged. He nodded. The verdict was the last thing he heard.

quests.trigger: A body with a note requesting a specific funeral rite.
quests.discovery: A body in a ditch, and in the pocket a note in careful handwriting: 'If found, please bury me facing east, with a stone on my chest. This is my faith.' The faith is not yours and you do not know it. The instructions are exact. The ground here is frozen half a spade down.

choices.label: Perform the rite as requested
choices.outcome_text: The frozen ground costs you two hours. You set the body facing east, find a flat stone, and lay it on the chest as written. You do not know the words, so you say none. It is done exactly, for a faith that is not yours, by a stranger.
choices.epitaph: Buried them facing east, stone on the chest, no words. Two hours in frozen ground. Done exactly, for a faith not mine.

choices.label: Bury them simply, no rite
choices.outcome_text: You dig and fill and set a marker, facing whichever way the ditch allowed. The note goes back in the pocket. They are buried, which is the main thing, you tell yourself. The stone they asked for stays in the field where it was.
choices.epitaph: Buried them plain, no east, no stone. Their note went back in the pocket. Buried is the main thing, I said.

choices.label: Bury them your way
choices.outcome_text: You bury them the way your own people do it, facing the shelter line, a handful of ash over the fill. It is a proper burial by your lights. Their paper asked for something else. You decide one faith is as good as another, which is easy to decide when it is not your body.
choices.epitaph: Buried them my way, ash and all. The paper asked otherwise. Easy to decide when it is not my body.

choices.label: Leave them, the rite is not yours
choices.outcome_text: You leave the body and its instructions where they lie. The rite is not yours to perform, you tell yourself, and a wrong burial might be worse than none. The frozen ditch keeps its careful handwriting.
choices.epitaph: Left the body and its instructions. A wrong burial might be worse than none, I said. The ditch keeps the handwriting.
